source_ambiguities.text: UNCERTAIN - generator, geometric region. The printed ratios are rounded to two decimal places and are NOT the generator: the ratios actually implied by row 1 are 1.1867, 1.1910, 1.1887, 1.1905, 1.1933, 1.1899, 1.1878, 1.1897 (printed as x1.19) and 1.2890, 1.3892, 1.4898, 1.5903, 1.6899 (printed as x1.29 .. x1.69). Iterating L(n+1) = round(L(n) * 1.19) from 150 drifts off the printed lengths within a few steps (it yields 358 -> 357, 426 -> 425, 776 -> 777, 4316 -> 4323), and so does iterating on an unrounded accumulator (4316 -> 4331). No simple closed form recovered from the figure reproduces row 1. CONSEQUENCE FOR IMPLEMENTERS: treat the 24 literal history lengths in row 1 as the authoritative data and hard-code them. Do not regenerate them from the first-difference row.

UNCERTAIN. The figure does not label the wire that selects x0 vs x2.5. The panel (a)/(b) analogy and the "largest / Most useful in this bank" output make the bank's own usefulness value the natural driver, but this is not drawn explicitly. The alternative reading - a single global static scale of 2.5 - is not consistent with an "x0" option existing at all, but cannot be ruled out from the figure alone.

UNCERTAIN - count encoding. Each count field is 6 bits, but a 64-bit register can have 0..64 leading (or trailing) identical bits, which needs 7 bits. The figure does not say whether the count saturates at 63, is taken modulo 64, or counts bits matching the sign bit (which caps at 63 naturally). The prose "the count of leading zeros (or ones)" also does not say how the zero/one case is distinguished - whether one extra bit encodes which, or whether the count is simply of bits equal to the MSB (resp. LSB).

UNCERTAIN. The right-alignment at bit 3 is read off the drawing, not stated. An alternative is that each format's field is right-aligned at bit 0. Also, the format-classification step ("we inspect the most significant bits to classify the format") is described only in prose; the figure does not show how the classification is performed, nor what happens for a value that is not a recognisable float.
